newsitem.title: UK: Wine world splashes out for Webber's cellar sale.
newsitem.headline: Wine world splashes out for Webber's cellar sale.

text.p: Wine lovers splashed out more than 3.5 million pounds ($5.8 million) for composer Andrew Lloyd Webber's prized collection on Wednesday, smashing pre-sale estimates and setting a world record for a wine auction.

"The magic combination of stunning, impeccable wines...combined with the incredible provenance clearly proved irresistible to buyers," said Serena Sutcliffe, head of the wine department at Sotheby's auction house.

The most spectacular item was the "Millennium Cellar Super Lot", a selection of some of the greatest wines ever produced, including champagnes, clarets and dessert wines described by Sotheby's as "a hedonist's paradise".
A Las Vegas hotel chain spent 242,000 pounds to secure the one imperial, three double magnums, two jeroboams, 77 magnums and 265 bottles for its cellars.
"We sell 2,000 bottles of wine a day and were running out. The wine we have bought...is for drinking," explained Barrie Larvin, master sommelier of the Rio Suite Hotel and Casino.
The two-day auction fetched a total of 3.7 million pounds, far surpassing the two million pound estimate.
Wines from the landmark 1947 vintage proved among the most coveted of the sale with three cases of Chateau Latour a Pomerol fetching 35,200 pounds.
A private European collector spent 121,000 pounds for 360 bottles of first growth Bordeaux, described as "truly mythical wine".
Small-pocketed connoisseurs could take heart at some of the lower priced items, including a case of 1988 Louis Roederer that sold for a mere 198 pounds.
After the auction, which he did not attend, Webber simply said: "I am obviously thrilled with the result."

When the Oscar-winning British composer was not writing hit musicals "Evita" and "Cats", he was putting together what Sotheby's called "the greatest single-owner wine collection ever to be offered at auction".
"It was the ultimate wine list," said Sutcliffe.

A self-styled incurable collector, Lloyd Webber first began buying wines as a schoolboy, gradually amassing a cellar of over 18,000 bottles, far more than even the most ambitious wine drinker could consume in a lifetime.
"I realise I have been hogging far too much of it. It is time to clear out," Lloyd Webber wrote in the introduction to the lavish catalogue resembling a theatre programme.

After cleaning house and taking inventory of his wine war chest, Lloyd Webber himself was astonished at what he discovered. "I was flabbergasted. Years of falling prey to all those tempting offers caught up with me. I needed to rationalise."
Despite the auction Webber has not given up his addiction to wines. He is back in the market buying young 1995 vintages from France and the New World.

But it was not without nostalgia that he parted with his prized collection. "I hope they find good loving homes, particularly those naughtily tannic Rhones and my beloved Burgundies," he said. "I shall miss you boys."
